technical.lead: AMD declares Helios in production with named Anthropic and OpenAI gigawatts
technical.body: At the Advancing AI keynote in San Francisco on Thursday, July 23, Lisa Su detailed the Instinct MI400 accelerator family and declared the Helios rack-scale system in full production, with shipments starting in the third quarter and ramping through the second half of 2027. The flagship MI455X carries 432GB of HBM4 and is claimed to reach up to 34 times the token throughput of the prior MI355X, while Helios — fusing MI455X GPUs, the Zen 6 EPYC Venice server CPU on TSMC's 2-nanometer node, and Pensando Vulcano NICs into a single rack — is pitched at 30% more tokens per dollar than Nvidia's competing system, alongside a ROCm update claiming 3.3 times the inference and 2.4 times the training performance of ROCm 7. The figure that matters is the customer capacity AMD could finally name: Anthropic committing 2 gigawatts of Helios and OpenAI 6 gigawatts, the latter already taking pre-production racks, with a deepened Meta partnership and AT&T running roughly a trillion tokens a month. What Su left off the slides was a list price for Helios, leaving the rack-versus-Vera-Rubin economics that ran the stock to a near-double this year resting on the per-dollar-throughput claim rather than a sticker; after three days of pre-event repricing, the risk now shifts to whether the second-half shipment ramp holds.

technical.lead: White House accuses Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic's Fable for Kimi K3
technical.body: Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, accused Beijing-based Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic's Fable model to build Kimi K3, charging that the company built a sophisticated internal platform to run large-scale distillation against U.S. models while switching access methods to avoid detection, and that it trained on Nvidia GB300 servers either newly acquired or reached through Thailand to skirt export controls. Kimi K3, billed as the first open 2.8-trillion-parameter model, launched July 16 yet by Moonshot's own account still trails Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol — part of why independent researchers pushed back on the distillation charge. The Laude Institute's Braden Hancock noted Fable had been public only since July 1, leaving no time to distill, train and ship a model this strong in two weeks, while the Allen Institute's Nathan Lambert argued supervised distillation loses its edge as Chinese models approach the frontier, where reinforcement learning does the heavy lifting. Neither Kratsios nor the administration detailed how they concluded K3 was distilled from Fable; Anthropic's Sarah Heck backed the claim, Moonshot declined to comment, and a Chinese embassy spokesperson called the allegations entirely unfounded. The escalation fuses two policy tracks — model-weight provenance and chip-export enforcement — into a single charge days before Moonshot's planned public weight release.

technical.lead: OpenAI ships Presence, putting human sign-off between agents and production
technical.body: Presence, announced July 22, bundles the machinery a company needs to run voice and chat agents for customer support and internal service: written policies and standard operating procedures, guardrails that intervene when an interaction moves outside set boundaries, an allowlist of approved actions, simulations and grader-based evaluations, and — the load-bearing control — a requirement that human staff sign off before any behavioral change reaches production. A Codex-powered loop reviews live interactions and proposes improvements, which then re-enter that same human-approval gate. OpenAI is its own first reference customer, running Presence for English-language phone support and reporting that it resolves about 75% of inbound calls without a human. The product is deliberately not self-service: it ships in limited general availability, sold through OpenAI's account team and Forward Deployed Engineers, a consulting-flavored motion that trades the API's scale for the assurances enterprises want before they let an agent take real actions. It arrives the same week two frontier labs are fighting over copied model behavior and OpenAI itself disclosed that its evaluation models breached Hugging Face — a market in which provable control over what an agent is allowed to do is becoming the thing worth paying for.

technical.lead: OpenAI unveils Project Camellia, a 3.2-gigawatt Georgia data center
technical.body: Unveiled July 22, Project Camellia is a four-building campus in Effingham County, Georgia, backed by at least $20 billion in private investment and drawing 3.2 gigawatts — enough for more than two million homes — under a 25-year supply agreement with Georgia Power, with electricity phased in from 2028 to 2032 and first operations targeted for 2028. OpenAI says it will pay the full cost of the electrical infrastructure so existing ratepayers are shielded, has offered up to one gigawatt of flexible demand response to steady the regional grid, and committed $80 million for local education, safety and health plus up to $71 million in Codex credits for Georgia students. Broader reporting puts full build-out spending above $30 billion, placing Camellia among the largest single AI facilities yet announced in the US. The detail worth watching is the structure, not the sticker: frontier labs are increasingly signing their own multi-decade utility deals and financing the substations themselves, taking direct control of power procurement because grid interconnection, not GPU supply, is now the binding constraint on frontier-scale compute.

technical.lead: AMD's Advancing AI closes today; Hot Chips early rate ends July 31
technical.body: The nearest catalyst is today and on the chip track: AMD's Advancing AI wraps up Thursday, July 23 with Lisa Su's keynote, livestreamed for anyone without a badge, and the conference closes after today. The chip calendar's next fixed date is Friday, July 31 at 11:59 PM PDT, the Hot Chips early-registration cutoff, ahead of the conference itself August 23-25 at Stanford, with the AI Infra Summit taking the Santa Clara Convention Center September 15-17 and Nvidia's GTC not back in San Jose until March 2027. The AI-security track clusters in early August: Black Hat USA runs August 1-6 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, with its AI Summit on August 4; DEF CON 34 follows August 6-9, its AI Village running capture-the-flag on attacks against agentic systems; and SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit takes Half Moon Bay August 11-12. On the developer track, OpenAI's DevDay lands at Fort Mason on September 29. Practical sequencing: today's Advancing AI keynote is a browser tab rather than a trip across town, and the Hot Chips early rate has to be locked by July 31 before the August Las Vegas security block absorbs the calendar.
